title: A Nd molecular butterfly: a unique all-in-one material for SMM, MCE and maiden photosensitized opto-electronic device fabrication

material_class.structural_family: coplanar hexanuclear Nd6 butterfly / three-blade propeller cage

synthesis.procedure: BMPC (53.5 mg) and Nd(NO3)3·6H2O (44 mg, 1 equiv. with respect to the ligand) were taken up in 5 ml of a 1:1 DMF–MeOH mixture and refluxed in a 100 ml round-bottom flask at 70–80 °C for 4–5 h. The resulting yellow solution was cooled to room temperature, filtered into a 10 ml beaker, covered, and left undisturbed. After about one week, rod-shaped bright yellow crystals formed, were collected, and washed with MeOH.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: 100 ml round-bottom flask reflux, then undisturbed crystallization in a covered 10 ml beaker
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Cool, filter into a 10 ml beaker, cover and leave undisturbed; collect rod-shaped bright yellow crystals and wash with MeOH.

properties.summary: Discrete Nd6 butterfly cluster showing field-induced SMM behaviour (Ueff = 3.4 K, τ0 = 3.1 × 10−4 s at 0.3 T) and a magnetocaloric entropy change of 8.28 J kg−1 K−1 at 3 K and 5 T. Thin-film UV–vis absorption (λmax ≈ 354 nm) gives an optical band gap of 3.05 eV; the complex was used in a photosensitized ITO/Nd6/Al Schottky diode.
